document.lead: You should spend about 20 minutes on this task.

text: The table compares the average number of hours per week that people in four age groups spent on physical exercise in 2000 and in 2020.
Overall, the youngest group became less active while all the older groups exercised more, so the differences between the age groups narrowed considerably over the two decades.

In 2000, adults aged 18–29 exercised most, for 6.5 hours a week, which was more than three times the figure for people aged 60 and over (1.9 hours). By 2020, however, this had dropped to 4.6 hours, the only decrease in the table. In that year, the difference between the youngest and the oldest group was 4.6 hours, which was the widest gap in the table.

The picture was reversed for older adults. The 45–59 group showed the biggest rise, from 2.8 to 4.9 hours, which meant that it overtook the youngest group to become the most active. Similarly, the figure for those aged 60 and over doubled to 3.8 hours, while the 30–44 group made only a modest gain of 0.4 hours, reaching 4.4.
